syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Understanding Society India and Beyond PART-II
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: Ocean Relief and Submarine Features
topics.ncert_sections: Ocean Relief; Important submarine relief features

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main features of the ocean floor such as the continental shelf, slope, abyssal plain, ridges and trenches.
Distinguish seamounts from guyots and explain how they are formed.

topics.title: Waves
topics.ncert_sections: Movement of Ocean Water: Waves

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the cause of waves and the parts of a wave such as crest, trough and wavelength.
Explain how wave erosion forms caves, arches, stacks and stumps along a coast.
Distinguish tsunamis from ordinary storm waves by their cause and effects.

topics.title: Tides
topics.ncert_sections: Tides; Spring Tides and Neap Tides

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the relative positions of the Sun, Earth and Moon produce spring and neap tides.
Explain the importance of tides for navigation, fishing and tidal energy.

topics.title: Ocean Currents
topics.ncert_sections: Ocean Currents

concepts.learning_objective: State the factors, including the Coriolis force, that cause ocean currents.
Analyse how warm and cold currents affect the climate of coastal regions.
Explain why the meeting zones of warm and cold currents are rich fishing grounds.

topics.title: Cyclones and Tsunamis: Early Warning Systems
topics.ncert_sections: Cyclones and Tsunamis: Early Warning Systems; Focus on Cyclones

concepts.learning_objective: Describe India's cyclone warning measures and the system of naming cyclones.
Explain how the tsunami early warning system detects, confirms and communicates threats.
Describe how the GEMINI device helps fishermen stay safe at sea.

topics.title: Marine Resources and the Blue Economy
topics.ncert_sections: Marine Resources and Their Significance; Blue Economy

concepts.learning_objective: Classify marine resources into living and non-living, and energy into conventional and non-conventional.
Explain the importance of marine resources for food, energy, trade and culture.
Evaluate actions in the light of the Blue Economy and SDG 14 Life Below Water.

topics.title: Maritime Zones and International Maritime Rules
topics.ncert_sections: Maritime Zones; International Maritime Rules and Regulations

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the extent of territorial sea, contiguous zone, EEZ and high seas under UNCLOS.
Apply the principles of innocent passage and flag-state law on the high seas.
State the purpose of maritime rules such as COLREGs and MARPOL.

topics.title: Biomes: meaning and the factors that shape them
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Types of Biomes

concepts.learning_objective: Define a biome and distinguish it from an ecosystem.
Identify the factors such as temperature and precipitation that decide which plants and animals a biome supports.

topics.title: Terrestrial biomes
topics.ncert_sections: Terrestrial Biomes: Forest, Grassland, Desert, Tundra

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the location and importance of tropical rainforests as a gene bank.
Compare grasslands and deserts in rainfall, vegetation and adaptations of life.
Explain how permafrost and cold limit life in the tundra.

topics.title: Aquatic biomes and the biome pyramid
topics.ncert_sections: Aquatic Biomes; Biome Pyramid

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish freshwater and marine biomes and state their importance.
Explain why number, biomass and energy decrease up the levels of a biome pyramid.

topics.title: Biodiversity and its geographical conservation
topics.ncert_sections: Interconnectedness between Biomes and Living Beings; Maintaining Ecological Balance and Biodiversity

concepts.learning_objective: Define biodiversity at the level of species, genes and ecosystems.
Explain hotspots, protected areas, ecosystem-based conservation and wildlife corridors.

topics.title: Forest ecotourism and forests as livelihoods
topics.ncert_sections: Forest Ecotourism; Forests and Livelihoods; Forest Dwellers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain ecotourism and evaluate the Thenmala model of community-based tourism.
Describe how forest dwellers depend on and protect forests, including sacred groves and forest movements.

topics.title: Geographical Indication of forest products
topics.ncert_sections: Geographical Indication (GI); GI-tagged Forest Products in India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what a GI tag is and how it benefits local communities.
Match GI-tagged forest products of India with their regions and features.

topics.title: Challenges of forest dwellers and government efforts
topics.ncert_sections: Challenges Faced by People Living in Forests; Government Efforts to Support Forest Dwellers; Mendha Lekha

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the problems faced by forest dwellers, such as disasters, fires and human-wildlife conflict.
Explain the Forest Rights Act, JFM and the Mendha Lekha model of community forest management.

topics.title: Ecological commons
topics.ncert_sections: Ecological Commons; Bihar fisheries; Water tanks

concepts.learning_objective: Define ecological commons and explain why they are shrinking.
Analyse commons-based fisheries in Bihar and traditional water tanks as collective resource management.

topics.title: Meaning of resistance and resilience; early resistance to invasions
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Safeguarding Sovereignty: Resistance, Alliances, and Confederacies

concepts.learning_objective: Define resistance and resilience and explain how they are interconnected.
Describe how Indian rulers resisted the Arab, Ghaznavid and Ghurid invasions of the 7th to 12th centuries.

topics.title: Rajput resistance against the Sultanate and the Mughals
topics.ncert_sections: Rajput Dynasties: Confederacies and Resistance; Rajput-Mughal Dynamics; Mewar's Resistance against Mughals

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Delhi Sultanate faced resistance from regional kingdoms and Rajput dynasties.
Distinguish between Rajput kingdoms that resisted the Mughals and those that negotiated cooperation.
Trace Mewar's resistance from the siege of Chittor to the treaty that recognised its autonomy.

topics.title: The Ahom kingdom and the Vijayanagara Empire
topics.ncert_sections: The Ahom Kingdom: Centuries of Endurance; Vijayanagara Empire: Resilience against Expansion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how terrain, the navy, the Paik system and leaders like Lachit Borphukan helped the Ahoms resist the Mughals.
Describe how the Vijayanagara Empire rose to check the Sultanate's expansion into peninsular India.
Interpret acts of symbolic defiance by the Nayaka rulers after Vijayanagara fragmented.

topics.title: Marathas, Sikhs and Jats
topics.ncert_sections: Marathas: The Quest for Swarajya; The Sikhs: A Story of Spiritual and Political Resilience; Jat Resistance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the idea of swarajya and the role of forts in Maratha resistance.
Describe how the martyrdom of the Gurus, the Akal Takht, miri-piri, the Khalsa and the misals shaped Sikh resilience.
Explain the causes and course of the Jat rebellions against the Mughals.

topics.title: The Bhakti tradition and spiritual resilience
topics.ncert_sections: Bhakti Tradition: Affirmation of the Spirit of Resilience; Sufism; Sulh-i-Kul

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main features and streams of the Bhakti tradition and its prominent saints.
Explain how non-material worship, local languages and community singing made Bhakti resilient.
Describe the spread of Sufism and the meaning of Akbar's policy of Sulh-i-kul.

topics.title: Temples: the resilience of sacred sites
topics.ncert_sections: Temples: The Resilience of Sacred Sites

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the economic, social and political functions of temples.
Explain how temples were restored and how the haveli-style design reflected adaptation.

topics.title: Economy: agriculture, trade networks and merchant communities
topics.ncert_sections: Indian Economy: Agriculture, Trading Networks, and Merchant Communities; The World of the Indian Ocean: Continuity and Change

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of land revenue and irrigation technologies in the agrarian economy.
Describe inland and seaborne trade networks and the use of the hundi as a financial instrument.
Analyse how Indian merchant groups adapted to the arrival of European trading companies.
Distinguish government as the institutions exercising political authority from governance as the process of making, implementing and monitoring decisions.
Explain why public problems need coordinated action by many institutions and citizens.
Identify Indian ideas of governance such as Sabha and Samiti, Rajadharma and Ram Rajya.
Relate national mottos and the Sengol to the values of good governance in India.

topics.title: Good governance, its challenges and e-governance

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the features of good governance such as transparency, accountability, rule of law and inclusiveness.
Analyse challenges such as weak coordination, unequal access, misuse of office and misinformation.
Explain how e-governance improves service delivery and why it must remain inclusive.
Explain public policy as a course of action adopted by the government to solve public problems.
Distinguish a public policy from the policy of an organisation or limited group.
Identify the roles of different stakeholders in policy-making and implementation.

topics.title: The making of a public policy

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the stages of the policy cycle from desirability to evaluation.
Describe how NEP 2020 was developed through expert advice and public consultation.
Distinguish a policy, a programme and a scheme using the National Health Policy 2017.

topics.title: Policy coordination: key to good governance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a policy like Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 depends on coordination across levels and stakeholders.
Evaluate how citizens strengthen governance by voting, following laws and giving feedback.

topics.title: Personal finance and its pillars: income
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Pillars of Personal Finance; Income (Earnings)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what personal finance means and why money must be managed efficiently.
Identify the five pillars of personal finance and what each involves.
Recognise different forms of income such as salary, profit, rent, interest and dividends.

topics.title: Budgeting and saving
topics.ncert_sections: Budgeting (Planning Expenses); Steps in Budgeting; Saving

concepts.learning_objective: Explain budgeting as planning in advance how income will be spent to balance income and expenses.
Apply the four steps of budgeting, including setting a savings goal.
Explain why people save a part of their income.

topics.title: Investing: inflation and the power of compounding
topics.ncert_sections: Investing (Growing Wealth); Power of Early Investments

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between keeping savings as cash and investing them in assets.
Explain how inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.
Analyse how compounding makes early investment more rewarding.

topics.title: Common investment options
topics.ncert_sections: Common Investment Options: Fixed Deposits, Bonds, Stocks, Mutual Funds

concepts.learning_objective: Describe fixed deposits and bonds and calculate the interest earned on them.
Explain that shares represent ownership and carry higher risk and potential return.
Explain how mutual funds pool money and reduce risk through diversification.

topics.title: Protection: insurance, borrowing and credit
topics.ncert_sections: Protection and Risk Management; Insurance; Types of Insurance; Borrowing and Credit

concepts.learning_objective: Explain insurance as a contract based on premiums and risk sharing.
Classify health, life and general insurance with examples.
Evaluate responsible borrowing and the meaning of an EMI.

topics.title: Risk and return
topics.ncert_sections: Risk and Return; Risk/Return Trade-Off

concepts.learning_objective: Identify risk, return, time horizon and liquidity as factors in investment decisions.
Analyse the trade-off between risk and return across investment options.

topics.title: Taxes and personal income tax
topics.ncert_sections: Taxes; Personal Income Tax; Tables 5.1 and 5.2

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between direct and indirect taxes with examples.
Explain progressive taxation and the slab system.
Calculate income tax using the standard deduction and the tax slabs.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship and the entrepreneur
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Fig. 6.1, 6.2; From a Dead Mouse to Riches

concepts.learning_objective: Explain entrepreneurship as the process of converting a potential idea into a business venture.
Identify the tasks an entrepreneur performs, such as combining factors of production and taking risks.
Interpret the Jataka tale to show how entrepreneurs spot opportunities and work smart.

topics.title: Entrepreneurial journeys: Lijjat and Oberoi
topics.ncert_sections: From Rooftop to Revolution; The Man who Transformed the Hospitality Industry

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Lijjat Papad grew as a women's cooperative with equal ownership and shared profits.
Explain how Mohan Singh Oberoi's initiative, risk-taking and management built a hotel chain.

topics.title: Business plan: a road map for the business
topics.ncert_sections: Business Plan - A Road Map for the Business; Fig. 6.6

concepts.learning_objective: Define a business plan as a written blueprint of goals and the steps to achieve them.
Apply the key considerations of a business plan (needs, customers, costs, location, pricing, promotion, risks) to a venture.

topics.title: Functional areas of a business
topics.ncert_sections: Functional Areas of a Business; Fig. 6.9; Management and Operations; Human Resources; Marketing and Sales

concepts.learning_objective: Name the four functional areas of a business and the key focus of each.
Classify business activities into management and operations, human resources, or marketing and sales.

topics.title: Finance and accounting
topics.ncert_sections: Finance and Accounting; Fig. 6.11

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between fixed costs and variable costs with examples.
Calculate profit from revenue and expenses using a profit and loss account.

topics.title: Traditional entrepreneurs, startups and the nation
topics.ncert_sections: India's Traditional Entrepreneurial Community; Startups and Their Contribution to the Nation; Fig. 6.13

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Chettiar community as a traditional entrepreneurial community and its practices.
Describe India's startup ecosystem, unicorns, failure as learning and schemes like Startup India.
Analyse how businesses contribute to society and the economy and to Viksit Bharat 2047.
